title: Optimize Evals - 1:1 Prep & Action Items (Mar 2026)
content:
Context / goal:
- Prep for 1:1 with Aisha on Optimize evals & recent quality regressions (quick sync: 20-30m).
- Focus: triage top regressions from last A/B, decide fixes (prompt changes / model pin / post-filter), and assign owners + timelines.
- Desired outcome: clear action list + next checkpoint (next weekly evals sync).

Quick summary (last A/B, run 2026-02-28):
- Test suite: 4 prompt sets (dialogue, summarization, extraction, instruction-following), ~8k eval pairs total.
- Primary signal: human-rated helpfulness (Likert) + automated BLEU/SARI where applicable.
- Overall: small but consistent drop in helpfulness on dialogue prompts vs baseline (delta -6.2%).
- Notable: extraction set stable; summarization noisy (high variance), instruction-following regressed for specific one-shot prompts.
- Perf/latency: p95 latency +5% on dedicated staging (likely unrelated, but note).

Key failing examples (to bring up):
1) Dialogue prompt: "Help me plan a 3-day trip to Kyoto"
   - Baseline output: coherent 3-day itinerary with times, transit tips (score 4/5).
   - New variant: terse, misses transit and timing, hallucinated wrong temple hours (score 2/5).
   - Notes: hallucinated hours are a regression we flagged in EVALS-212.

2) Instruction-following (one-shot): "Convert this spec into a checklist for QA" + example
   - Baseline: clear checklist with discrete items.
   - New: combines items into paragraphs, misses two critical checks (security headers).
   - Impact: product teams rely on checklist output for onboarding; severity = medium.

Hypotheses (quick):
- Kernel / quantization change in model binary may have affected long-range coherence (related PR: optimize/pull/278).
- Prompt templating change (we switched to new system-level instruction formatting last week) reduced priming effectiveness for some one-shot prompts.
- Data shuffle: sampling for rolling evals inadvertently dropped some rare prompt variants => evaluation noise.

Immediate triage plan (what I want to confirm in 1:1):
- Re-run failing prompts against prior pinned model commit (A) vs current (B) + one intermediate (C) to isolate regression commit range.
- Sanity-check prompt formatting: compare old vs new template on a small sample (10 examples).
- Check CI for optimize/pull/278 for any model-packaging flags toggled.
- Ask SRE: did any infra changes (CUDA, libraries) happen on staging nodes between 2026-02-20 and 2026-02-27?

Proposed action items (assignments + target dates):
- Re-run focused A/B/C (10k items subset) and produce diff report (owner: Casey Lee) - due 2026-03-05.
- Narrow failing prompts list + canonical examples (owner: Jamie Park) - due 2026-03-03.
- Prompt template rollback test (run old template vs new on 200 examples) (owner: Aisha Khan) - due 2026-03-04.
- Inspect PR optimize/pull/278 and bubble up suspicious flags to eng (owner: Lena Roberts) - due 2026-03-04.
- Open a regression incident if A/B shows model-level regression beyond prompt fix (owner: Jamie Park) - decision due 2026-03-06.

Longer-term items (not for this 1:1, but log):
- Add targeted coverage for one-shot instruction prompts into the rolling evals (owner: optimize team, tracked in EVALS-230).
- Improve regression detection sensitivity (reduce noise in summarization set).

Open questions to discuss in 1:1:
- If regression is model-level, do we prefer to rollback model version for hosted customers or apply prompt-specific mitigations? Tradeoffs: cost vs risk.
- Should we expand human-rating density for high-variance summarization set? Budget implications.
- How to surface regressions to product owners faster (Slack alerts / email)?

Notes-to-self (things to remember during sync):
- Bring the three canonical failing examples (dialogue, instruction, summarization) and have raw outputs ready.
- Keep convo tight: focus on root cause triage steps and owners.
- If infra change found, escalate to SRE and pause rollout windows.

Next steps after 1:1:
- Send a short recap in #optimize-evals with action items, owners, and due dates (I will draft).
- Schedule quick follow-up checkpoint (15m) on 2026-03-06 to review Casey's diff report.

References / quick links for the meeting:
- Regression heatmap (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/optimize-regression-heatmap
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/278
- Jira: EVALS-212 (dialogue hallucination regression)
- Slack thread: #optimize-evals (thread ts: G12345)

TODO (personal):
- Prepare 3 slides for leadership summary if we need to escalate (1) impact, (2) root-cause hypotheses, (3) proposed mitigations + timeline.
- Double-check human rater notes for the most egregious dialogue examples (ask ops for raw rater comments).

-- jamie
